about: Every difference between cua's output and the vendor's on these goldens, each with its cause (PROVENANCE.md). `fault` names where it comes from: "engine" (the recorded Skyshot is wrong, or lacks what the vendor reads), "redaction" (Finder's captures hide the content the rule reads) "scene state" (the two lanes' actions left different states) or "engine or renderer" (undecided until M1b compares Finder by full text). The engine corrections (`kind: "skyshot"`, fault "engine") and the engine differences expire: M1b re-records these goldens live from the fixed engine (task M1a.2b) and deletes every engine-fault declaration then; one still needed at that point is an engine defect, not a declaration. Kinds: `skyshot` (a correction applied to the Skyshot before rendering), `part` (inside a matched line, cua's `<label>: <cua>` is the vendor's `<label>: <vendor>`), `missing` and `added` (a whole line, by its matching key), `header` and `trailer` (both sides' exact text), `addedOverTenPercent` (`decisionLog` cites the entry by its dated opening, `- Decision (<YYYY-MM-DD>…`). `golden` is "full", "before" or "diff" (all three when absent); `count` is exact.

declarations.cause: Engine (the flag's derivation): the recordings set flags.disclosable whenever AXDisclosing is present, where the vendor's isDisclosable is AXDisclosing supported and settable (FUN_10074cb90, in get_app_state's fullUIContext; isDisclosing is its value). No vendor line in any capture prints `collapsed`: every web element of Chrome and Electron carries AXDisclosing false, and so do Finder's leaf rows and every menu-bar item, where the vendor prints neither flag nor an Expand action; the vendor prints `expanded` on Finder's expanded sidebar sections. The recordings do not carry settability, so the correction keeps the flag only where the element is expanded. Fixed in the engine in M1a.2b.

Engine (the flag's derivation): the recordings carry AXUIElementIsAttributeSettable(AXValue), which Chromium answers true for nearly every native view and web control. In a Chromium window (the context's isChromium: web-shaped and the window's first child lists ChromeAXNodeId, FUN_100747dac) the vendor reads AXValue's settability only for the roles of FUN_10074ff74 (AXComboBox, AXIncrementor, AXTextArea, AXTextField; an incrementor of a date or time field excluded) and a tab, AXRadioButton with subrole AXTabButton (FUN_100751614, called from FUN_10074cb90); every other element is not settable. The correction applies that rule; fixed in the engine in M1a.2b.
Engine, as Chrome's entry: Electron's windows are Chromium's (isChromium), and the vendor reads settability on the text area only of the elements whose recordings answer settable (FUN_100751614).

Engine (the Skyshot shape): the recordings name every CFNumber "number", so a float whose value is integral renders `settable, integer` where the vendor prints `settable, float`: its valueTypeName (FUN_10074a794) is the CFNumber's own type by CFNumberIsFloatType, from the table float, integer, boolean, string, date, unknown (TextEdit's two ruler markers at 0, Finder's scroll bars and value indicators at 0 and its splitter at 177, each Finder line's length fitting `float`). The roles are the ones the captures show, since the recordings lost the type. Since M1a.2b the engine carries the vendor's name, which the renderer prints.

Engine (the Skyshot shape): the recordings carry the menu bar's top-level items and not the AXMenuBar element, which the vendor reads as a node of its own and prints after the window's tree with the items under it, the first (the Apple menu) and any titled `Debug` never read (`addMenuBarWithImmediateItems` 0x1007569b8); the renderer no longer synthesizes it. Since M1a.2b the engine emits the element and leaves the Apple menu out. The correction gives the element no role description, as the vendor's `menu bar` word implies (roleWord FUN_1006156c8 prints it only for a nil role description); that the bar, read through the attributes it lists (FUN_1007542cc), answers none is a hypothesis M1b's live text decides.

Engine (the flag's derivation): the recordings mark every menu-bar item selectable (AXSelected settable), where the vendor's isSelectable is never true for a menu item or a menu-bar item (FUN_10077d1e4); the renderer now prints menu-bar items through the ordinary line, which would print `(selectable)`. Fixed in the engine in M1a.2b.

Engine (the read set): the vendor prints the window's document as `URL: file:///…/cua-scene.rtf`: a window without AXURL takes its AXDocument, parsed as a URL (FUN_10074cb90). The recordings' window node has no url (AXURL was read, AXDocument was not). Fixed in the engine in M1a.2b.

Engine (the read set), as TextEdit's entry: the vendor prints the window's `URL: 127.0.0.1:<port>/`, its AXDocument (FUN_10074cb90). The URL set here is the cua run's page (the browser root view's url in the same Skyshot); the two lanes served the page on different ports. Fixed in the engine in M1a.2b.

Redaction, not rendering: the renderer drops an identifier that starts with `_` or `NS` [B §6], but the Finder captures replaced every identifier by its length, so the prefix is hidden and cua prints `ID: ⟨n⟩` where the vendor prints nothing. Twelve elements per lineage (the scene's skyshot.json, and the action pair's): the two scroll areas, an outline and the two scroll bars, whose 5-to-7-character identifiers fit `_NS:<n>`, and the seven menu-bar items after the Apple menu, whose 8-character identifiers fit `_NS:<nnnn>` (TextEdit's unredacted menu-bar items carry `_NS:839` and its kin; the menu bar prints them since M1a.2b, when the renderer took the vendor's ordinary line for its items); each vendor line fits only without the part, and each token is needed. Every other identifier prints on both sides.

declarations.cua: Scroll Left, Scroll Right, Scroll Up, Scroll Down
declarations.cause: Engine (the Skyshot shape): the vendor's filterActions (FUN_100782c24) keeps AXScrollLeftByPage and AXScrollRightByPage only on an element that answers AXHorizontalScrollBar, and AXScrollUpByPage and AXScrollDownByPage only on one that answers AXVerticalScrollBar. Each of Finder's two scroll areas has a vertical scroll bar only, so the vendor prints `Scroll Up, Scroll Down`, 22 characters (the table's words, FUN_100783260, the same in any language; each line's length without its hidden `_NS` identifier); TextEdit's has both and the vendor prints all four there. The recordings do not carry which scroll bars an element has, so the renderer keeps all four. Since M1a.2b the engine carries them (Node.scrollBars) and the renderer applies the rule.

declarations.cua: Window: "cua scene page - Chrome for Testing", App: Google Chrome for Testing.
declarations.cause: Engine (the window title): the vendor's header names the window "cua scene page" (the page's title) while the recordings' Skyshot.window.title, the window element's AXTitle in both lanes, is "cua scene page - Chrome for Testing". The vendor's title is `ApplicationWindow.title` 0x10076e174: the window server's name for the window (kCGWindowName), else its AXTitle, and "Desktop" for an untitled Finder window at the desktop-icon level; Chrome names its window by the page. Since M1a.2b the engine takes the same rule. The window server shows other processes' window names only under Screen Recording, so without that grant the engine prints the AX title, as the vendor does.

declarations.vendor: The focused UI element is 3 HTML 콘텐츠 cua Electron fixture, URL: file:///Users/new/Library/Caches/cua-harness/electron-fixture/44.9.0-012125d3c853/cua%20Electron%20Fixture.app/Contents/Resources/app/index.html
declarations.cause: Engine (the focused element), cause a hypothesis: the recordings' Skyshot.focused is null in every Electron capture of the cua lane, so cua's text has no trailer, where the vendor names the web area (before the click) and the clicked button (after it). The vendor's read is the engine's: the application's AXFocusedUIElement and nothing else, an absent value tolerated (`focusedUIElementContext` 0x100774a9c). The recording does not say which of two things happened: the app-level read answered nothing, or it answered an element the walk had not tokened (the recording engine left `focused` null in both cases). If the read answered nothing, the hypothesis is that the lanes' activation histories differ, the vendor's clicks activating the app (#162) and an Electron app that was never active answering no application-level focus; the recordings' own AXFocused flags are set, on the text area before the click and on the clicked button after it. If it answered an element outside the walk, the gap is the engine's: the vendor adds the focused element's branch to its tree (focusTree 0x100755388), which the engine does not. Since M1a.2b the engine records which (timings.focusRead: an AXError or `notAnElement`, else `outsideTheWalk`); M1b's live re-recording decides it.

Engine, cause a hypothesis: after the click the vendor's line for row 005's name field grows by exactly the 10 characters of `selected, ` (`(settable)` → `(selected, settable)`), the field reading selected; the cua lane's after-Skyshot reports the row and its four cells selected and the field not (AXSelected false, no traits). The vendor's isSelected is the engine's, AXSelected else the selected trait of AXTraits (FUN_10074cb90), so the predicate does not explain it. The hypothesis: Finder reports the name field selected only while its selection is emphasized, with Finder active (the vendor's click activates the app, #162); the redaction hides any other difference. M1b's live re-recording decides it.
